articles.title: Man United vs Ipswich Town: Premier League – preview, team news, prediction
articles.summary: United put in a sorry display as they lost 2-0 to Hull last weekend, while newly promoted Ipswich beat Sunderland 2-1.
articles.body:
Who: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town What: English Premier League Where: Old Trafford, Manchester, United Kingdom When: Sunday, August 30, at 4:30pm (15:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 12:30 GMT before our live text commentary stream

United face Ipswich Town with the hosts badly in need of a win after a shock defeat in their opening game.

Michael Carrick was rewarded with the United job on a permanent basis after guiding the Red Devils to third in the Premier League last season during an interim spell in charge.

However, the new campaign got off to the worst possible start for Carrick with a 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull last weekend.

Meanwhile, Ipswich, who were also promoted from the Championship last season, got off to a dream start in their first game of the season, winning 2-1 at home to Sunderland.

Ipswich also saw off Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup in midweek and will fancy their chances of springing an upset against the Red Devils.

A defeat for United would see them become the first team in Premier League history to start a season with back-to-back losses against promoted sides.

Carrick’s side gets early reality check at Hull

United ⁠arrived in Hull on Saturday ⁠riding a wave of optimism that had not washed over Old Trafford for years. But they were ripped to shreds by the rampant Tigers as first-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy caused a shock at the MKM Stadium.

United were toothless in attack and inept at the back, a fatal combination that allowed promoted Hull to celebrate their return to the Premier League after a nine-year absence – and a first league win over United for 52 years.

“We have a bit to improve on; it was never going to be perfect. Going behind makes it more difficult, against a promoted team at home,” Carrick said after the game.

He added: “It is one ‌game. ‌First game of the season. It is disappointing enough, it hurts, of course it does.

“But it doesn’t change the whole course of direction the team is going in or the football club. We will stay calm, stay in the bubble and focus on next week.”

New United signing Baleba out for three weeks

Carrick said Carlos Baleba will be unable to make his Manchester United debut for about three weeks due to an ankle injury, but that he is excited by the Cameroonian’s “massive potential”.

Baleba’s 70-million-pound ($95m) move from Brighton further bolstered Carrick’s midfield options after the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

But United could have to wait until October to see Baleba in action as he faces a race against time to return before a three-week international break next month.

“He’s got a little ankle issue, so maybe a couple of weeks or so, maybe three weeks. We’ll see but we knew that before, so it’s no major issue but it’ll be great to have him back when we can,” Carrick said at his pre-match news conference before Ipswich’s visit.

“We’re delighted to have Carlos. I think [he has] huge potential, massive potential. I think he’s a really exciting signing for us.

“I think the quality that he has, the attributes that he has that offsets a little bit of the balance of the group that we’ve got. Different strengths, different combinations.”

Ipswich earn cathartic win in first game of season

Jack Clarke’s late strike secured a cathartic victory last ⁠Saturday for Ipswich Town, whose 2-1 win over Sunderland underscored the club’s desire to shake off the ⁠memories of a dismal 2024-25 Premier League campaign.

Ipswich won only once after December 2024 as their return to ⁠the top flight following two decades in the lower tiers ended in a 19th-place finish and relegation back to the Championship.

But the club earned another promotion last season, and marked their ‌return to the big time with a victory that drew an emotional response from the roaring crowd at Portman Road.

“They pushed us on, they kept us going … We finished really strong and that’s a credit to the fans,” Ipswich captain Dara O’Shea, who has been at ⁠the club since 2024, said.

Ipswich won ⁠only once at Portman Road in the 2024-25 Premier League campaign, which started with a 10-game winless streak.

But the stadium has been hard to breach ⁠for visitors in the last year, with Ipswich unbeaten in home league games since ⁠October 2025.

“It took the club a ⁠long time to win last time in the Premier League so to put one on the board is nice. But one win won’t get ‌us where we need to get to,” said manager Gary O’Neil.

The Opta supercomputer has made Manchester United the favourites, with a win probability of 66.4 percent. Ipswich were given a 15.3 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a likelihood of 18.3 percent.

The two clubs only faced each other for the first time in 1958 and have now played 59 times, with United winning 30 games, Ipswich winning 19, and 10 matches ending as draws.

Ipswich have not beaten United since 1997, when the Tractor Boys shocked Alex Ferguson’s Red Devils 2-0 in the third round of the League Cup.

February 26, 2025: Man Utd 3-2 Ipswich (Premier League)

November 24, 2024: Ipswich 1-1 Man Utd (Premier League)

September 23, 2015: Man Utd 3-0 Ipswich (League Cup third round)

April 27, 2002: Ipswich 0-1 Man Utd (Premier League)

September 22, 2001: Man Utd 4-0 Ipswich (Premier League)

What happened the last time the two clubs met?

Harry Maguire’s header earned 10-man Manchester United a 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town in February 2025, a victory that pulled then manager Ruben Amorim’s struggling side clear of the Premier League relegation zone.

Amorim had endured a miserable time since joining the club the previous November, especially at home, with more Old Trafford pain on the cards after woeful defending let Jaden Philogene in for Ipswich’s early opener.

United responded well, however, and turned the match on its head as an own goal from Ipswich captain Sam Morsy and Matthijs de Ligt’s close-range finish put the hosts in front after 26 minutes.

The game swung again when United defender Patrick Dorgu was sent off two minutes before the break for a late lunge on Omari Hutchinson and the 10 players conceded almost immediately, with Philogene again the Ipswich scorer.

With the visitors having all the second half to make their numerical advantage count, it was Maguire who settled the match just after the interval to earn United the win.

Baleba, Amad Diallo, Tom Heaton, Matthijs de Ligt, Mason Mount and Manuel Ugarte are all set to miss United’s first home match of the season through injuries, with Ugarte potentially out until next season with a torn knee ligament.

articles.summary: El cuarteto formado por Cayetano García, Pablo Martínez, Manuel Fontán y Diego Domínguez acaban terceros al igual que Arévalo en la final de K1 200
articles.body: España sumó otras dos medallas en la segunda jornada de finales del Campeonato del Mundo, que se está disputando en la localidad polaca de Poznan. Carlos Arévalo, en K1 200, y el C4 500, formado por Cayetano García, Pablo Martínez, Manuel Fontán y Diego Domínguez acabaron terceros sus respectivas carreras para colgarse el bronce. En una distancia que no forma del programa olímpico, el K1 200, Arévalo se mostró solvente desde el inicio. El español supo aguantar el empuje del italiano Di Liberto, que protagonizó una salida fulgurante, para mantenerse en las plazas que daban acceso al podio. Así pudo ratificar en los metros finales el bronce, en 34.98, por detrás del italiano, que alcanzó la meta en 34.15 y el serbio Dragosavljevic, plata, con 34.72. Minutos más tarde, en la última final de la jornada, el C4 500, que tampoco es distancia olímpica, firmó otro bronce en una gran regata en la que fueron de menos a más. Cayetano García, Pablo Martínez, Manuel Fontán y Diego Domínguez sellaron una buena salida y lograron superar al equipo B de Rusia, finalmente cuarto, ya en el ecuador de la carrera (1:30.97). De hecho, se quedaron a sólo 28 milésimas de la plata, que ocupó el otro cuarteto ruso. El oro fue para el potente barco húngaro (1:29.44). En las otras finales de la jornada, Angels Moreno y Viktoria Yarchevska, que también aspiraban a las medallas en C2 200, se quedaron a un paso del podio, al acabar cuartas con 42.97. El oro fue para las rusas Trushkina y Nedelkina, mientras que completaron el podio las uzbekas y China. En las finales B, Paco Cubelos y Diego Domínguez fueron segundos en K1 1.000 y C1 500, respectivamente, mientras que Claudia Couto acabó cuarta en C1 500 y Carolina García ganó la final C de K1 500. En paracanoe, Araceli Menduina fue cuarta a ocho centésimas del bronce en KL3 200 metros y Carlota Blanca e Higinio Rivero, octavos en KL2 200 y VL2 200.

articles.body: Can you believe we are already there? We've reached that point in the year when we have football once again. North Carolina was rocked in head coach Bill Belichick's first game at the helm. They looked lost on both offense and defense and fell 48-14. The rest of the campaign wasn't much better as the team had a 4-8 record overall. Looking at their wins, there really weren't any that were overly impressive, either. The reason for optimism this season is around Jaden Craig taking over under center. He comes over from Harvard, where he was successful, but the team wasn't very good. Jeremy Payne will be the featured back and could make this a dangerous backfield after a strong 2025. I like the chances of seeing some good offense from TCU. I don't love the total for the game, as I think it probably goes under 46.5, but we've already lost three points from the opening number. I am instead just focused on the TCU team total. San Jose State vs. USC There aren't a ton of lopsided games on the slate for today, but this is certainly one of them. San Jose State is expected to be blown out to start the year. USC has manhandled the Spartans in the past, having crushed them in their past three matches. Collectively, USC has won the last three matchups by a score of 146-38. articles.title: Instant Analysis: QB Sam Howell falls short in Cowboys loss; did he earn roster spot?
articles.summary: Sam Howell came up short in the Cowboys' 27-24 preseason finale loss, but he may have changed the team's plan at QB behind Dak Prescott.
articles.body:
Friday's preseason finale gave Cowboys coaches a good look at how their bubble players will- or won't- perform under pressure, with several prospects likely tipping the scales one way or the other toward earning a roster spot.

The Cowboys came up short in a 27-24 loss to New Orleans to just miss going undefeated in the preseason, but quarterback Sam Howell showed plenty of grit and fight in leading the team back from a 15-point deficit in the second half of action from AT&T Stadium to tie the score late.

Howell put up a better half of football than Joe Milton, going 12-of-18 passing for 155 yards and pair of touchdowns and also running in the two-point conversion that evened the score at 24-24 with six minutes to play. The 25-year-old actually had a perfect passer rating at that point, but going 2-for-7 on the offense's failed final drive dropped him to a 130.6 for the game. It's debatable whether he wrestled the QB2 job away from Milton, but he may well have proved himself worthy of keeping around.

The Dallas run game was rather lackluster, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind the trio of Phil Mafah, Israel Abanikanda, and Jashaun Corbin. Mafah got most of the work, with 12 attempts, and despite his 3.8 yards per tote, looked stronger than his numbers might indicate behind an offensive line of depth hopefuls.

Several receivers stood out. Jordan Hudson in particular showed a nice connection with Howell, posting nearly 100 yards and scoring on a toe-tap touchdown in the fourth quarter. Anthony Smith, Tyler Johnson, and Marquez Valdes-Scantling all caught multiple balls, though they all face long odds to make the 53-man roster due to sheer numbers. Preseason hero Camden Brown added just one catch to his totals, but it was another acrobatic grab that only helped his case for making the team.

At tight end, Zack Kuntz hasn't seemed to click with the offense since being signed earlier in the month. Rookie Michael Trigg, working his way back from a toe injury, had three bad drops on three decent targets. And Mitch Van Vooren hauled in a touchdown even though he only joined the team on Monday. How the Cowboys handle the TE group will be fascinating.

Defensively, Dallas allowed the Saints to convert just three of their nine third-down tries, but New Orleans found other ways to inflict damage. Christian Parker's B- and C-teams had trouble getting off the field overall, giving up five drives of 40 yards or more, all of which ended in points.

The Cowboys were sloppy against the run, as the Saints posted 5.3 yards per attempt on the night, had five different players rip off a ground gain in the double digits, and tallied rushing three touchdowns.

In the end, the preseason finale- for any team- is the rare instance where how the team performs as a whole isn't nearly as important as which individual players proved they belong. Friday's 27-24 exhibition loss will be forgotten soon by the Cowboys' fanbase. But it will have been enough to extend the NFL dream for a handful of hopefuls... and likely haunt almost 40 men who will no longer be on the team come Monday.

Todd is on X at @ToddBrock24f7 . Also, follow Cowboys Wire on Facebook to join in on the conversation with fellow fans!

articles.title: Super sub Reid nets late winner for Crues against Glens
articles.summary: Crusaders substitute Aaron Reid scores an 88th minute winner to secure a 2-1 win and all three points for Declan Caddell's side after a dogged display over G...
articles.body:
Crusaders substitute Aaron Reid scored an 88th minute winner to secure a 2-1 win for Declan Caddell's side after a dogged display over Glentoran at the Oval.

Owen Wardell put the visitors in front in the first half, before Ben Gallagher equalised on 68 minutes.

It looked like the hosts looked more likely to score again, but it was at the other end where Reid finished to secure all three points for Crusaders.

While there will be smiles all around for Declan Caddell, whose side have now won their past three games, Declan Devine will be wondering how Glentoran lost after creating a raft of chances throughout.

With just two minutes on the clock the Glens threatened first when a long diagonal ball from right to left was headed back across goal by Joshua Daniels before Gallagher fired just wide.

On 18 minutes Daniels again was causing problems for the visitors when he crossed superbly from the left into the path of Ryan Cooney, who made a great run from deep, but he just couldn't quite get his toe on the ball, and it ran behind for a goal-kick.

Three minutes later, Josh Kelly looped in a cross from the right for the hosts that cannoned off the underside of the crossbar.

Gallagher then found himself free six-yards out, but his shot was miraculously cleared off the line by a sliding Graham Kelly in the Crusaders defence.

Wardell went close for the Crues soon after, but he couldn't hit the target when clear through on goal.

Back at the other end, Ross Clarke had the goal at his mercy from five yards, however, the winger failed to head towards goal and the ball was cleared.

Then, just two minutes before the break and against the run of play, Elliot Dunlop drove down the left and crossed from the bye-line and there was Wardell to tuck home at the back post.

Glentoran grabbed an equaliser just after the hour mark when substitute Joe Thomson gave the ball to Cooney down the right and his inch-perfect cross found Gallagher at the back post and he headed home much to the delight of the home fans at the Oval.

However, Crusaders were not done and, with two minutes remaining, substitute Reid rounded Billy Crellin at the left post before slotting home from an acute angle to grab all three points.

articles.title: WRC Paraguay: Sami Pajari extends lead as storm damages service park
articles.summary: Sami Pajari has increased his Rally Paraguay lead as heavy rain hits the service park
articles.body:
Toyota's Sami Pajari has extended his Rally Paraguay lead to 22.8s as the anticipated heavy rain avoided the stages and instead struck the service park causing damage to several team facilities.

Heavy rain was expected which prompted teams to set up their cars for wet conditions, and it appeared to be the correct call as strong winds and heavy rain struck the service park on Saturday morning. The winds wreaked havoc, felling several team tents and even moving some of the sturdier temporary WRC team structures. Amazingly, the rain didn't arrive on the gravel stages to the surprise of the crews.

After ending Friday with an 11.9s lead over Hyundai's Hayden Paddon , Pajari managed to take time out of his Hyundai rival on three of the four stages to return to service with a healthy lead.

Pajari was however fortunate after surviving a scare in stage 11 when he ran wide in a ditch and damaged the rear wing of his Toyota GR Yaris.

"I guess it [the moment] was quite spectacular looking from the outside, but from the inside it didn't feel too massive. I didn't expect to have any damage so it was a big surprise to hear that the wing was damaged. The wing is not there only for the looks so I struggled a bit on the last stage, but it was not so bad," Pajari told Motorsport.com.

"It has been a good morning so I need to be happy with that."

Hayden Paddon, John Kennard, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

With his Hyundai i20 N set up for wet weather, Paddon struggled to replicate the speed and feeling he experienced in the dry on Friday and lost time in his fight with Pajari.

"I looked at a webcam on my phone before leaving the hotel and it looked like a hurricane had gone through the service park. It looked pretty horrendous. So the biggest thought is obviously with all the small teams. But it's amazing as out on the stages it has been fine and we didn't see a drop of rain. It was very weird," said Paddon.

"The whole mindset was for wet conditions. The car was set up for wet. It was a set up that I've never driven before."

Championship leader Elfyn Evans was glad the storm that hit the service park didn't affect the stages. The Toyota driver managed to win stage nine, the first of the morning loop, as he headed back to midday service in third, 54.1s from the lead.

"I think everybody feels a slight sense of relief on that side [the rain didn't arrive on the stages]," Evans told Motorsport.com.

"There's other areas that maybe we didn't perform as well as we could have or should have [running a wet set up]. Of course, after what happened yesterday with all these punctures, which was so rough, we were just trying to get through without issue."

Adrien Fourmaux, Alexandre Coria, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Hyundai's Adrien Fourmaux claimed two of the four morning stages as the Frenchman remained in fourth overall, but closed the gap to third-placed Evans to 31.8s.

M-Sport-Ford's Josh McErlean struggled to wrestle his Puma, set up for the wet, in the dry gravel stages but managed to hold on to fifth spot, although the gap to sixth-placed Oliver Solberg was cut to 35.6s.

M-Sport was the Rally1 team that suffered the most damage to its service area due to the storm and has had to take down its tents and relocate to another tent that it has rented for the event.

"We just took it all back down and put it in another tent that we've rented. A bit of proper rallying," M-Sport-Ford team principal Rich Millener told Motorsport.com. "I think the lucky thing is that there was nobody here in the service park because it was quite dangerous.

"We're working in a not ideal service park right now but it will be OK."

Home hero Diego Dominguez continued to lead the WRC2 standings, sitting in seventh overall despite forgetting his glasses at the end of stage 11.

articles.title: 100 Days to Kickoff: Opponent Previews – Louisville
articles.summary: The Jackets will host the Louisville Cardinals for their ninth game of the 2026 campaign, and to many, the matchup doesn’t make the shortlist of the season’s...
articles.body:
The Jackets will host the Louisville Cardinals for their ninth game of the 2026 campaign, and to many, the matchup doesn't make the shortlist of the season's most exciting bouts. The back-to-back primetime matchups against Colorado and Tennessee, the tough road tests against hungry Virginia Tech and Clemson squads, and, of course, COFH, all seem more interesting on paper than a home midseason matchup against the Cardinals. Yet by season's end, Louisville has a real shot at being the best team the Jackets face this year.

Cardinals football may be the most interesting thing about the otherwise lame city of Louisville. They joined the ACC in 2014 and firmly established themselves as a great, but not amazing ACC squad. This all changed in 2022, when the Cardinals hired head coach Jeff Brohm. Brohm, who once quarterbacked for Louisville in the 90s, is one of the best offensive minds in the biz. He's best known for leading Western Kentucky to its two greatest seasons ever and giving Purdue three of its six winning seasons since I have been, well, alive.

The Brohm show made a quick impact in its pilot season, as the Cardinals started 10-1 and had a decent shot at the College Football Playoff. They then completely collapsed, losing to a bad Kentucky team, the Jordan Travis-less Seminoles, and Caleb Williams' 7-5 USC in the Holiday Bowl. Ever since that first season, the Cardinals have been a perennially popular dark-horse pick for the CFP and ACC Championship, although they have not yet reached those heights.

2024 and 2025 were two different flavors of underachievement. In 2024, Louisville lost three of four matchups to CFP contenders, all by one score, with the death blow being an embarrassing loss to a terrible Stanford team. In 2025, the opposite happened: Louisville got an early marquee win against #2 Miami, but then lost three straight to unranked Cal, Clemson, and SMU.

This year, however, the expectations are even higher, as oddsmakers have Louisville as the second-most likely ACC Champion.

What gives Louisville upside to make it over the hump? It starts with Brohm, a QB whisperer who somehow manages to turn a different castaway signal-caller into a quality starter each season. His best achievement was turning Tyler Shough, a seventh year QB who had yet not played a complete season into a second-round pick who now starts for the Saints. This year, Lincoln Kienholz is the next project, who spent the last year holding the clipboard at Ohio State. While Kienholz is the least experienced of the QBs Brohm has brought in, Brohm scheme should at least keep him replacement level, with the upside of being a top 5 ACC QB.

As for the rest of the offense, the running backs should shine, with Isaac and Keyjuan Brown (no relation) leading the charge. Isaac Brown is a bona fide star, averaging a CFB-leading 7.1 and 8.8 yards per carry in his freshman and sophomore seasons. While Isaac Brown was hobbled towards the end of last year, Keyjuan Brown took over, averaging 7.3 yards per carry. While Isaac will be the obvious starter, Keyjuan provides a two-headed-monster dynamic that can vastly simplify the load on Kienholz.

Louisville won't have a wide receiver or tight end reach Isaac Brown's level of stardom this year, but pass catchers won't be an issue for the Cardinals either. The biggest names, Tre Richardson, Lawayne McCoy, and Brody Foley, all come from the transfer portal. Richardson was Vanderbilt's leading receiver last year, a big-play threat that averaged 17.5 yards per reception. McCoy has had a quieter career thus far, catching just 33 passes in two years with Florida State. Still, he has immense upside, as his value may be understated due to FSU's horrible offense. Then there is Brody Foley: the Tulsa product that is the third-highest ranked tight end transfer on 247Sports. Foley racked up the most receiving yards for the Golden Hurricanes last year and will likely hear his name called in the early rounds of the April draft.

While Louisville's skill positions aren't exactly stacked with depth, they should be good enough to provide relief in the case of injury without totally kneecapping the operation. The same doesn't go for the O-line. Louisville returns only Lance Robinson, a veteran leader who is in his seventh year. 2025 was his best season, where he notched an All-ACC honorable mention. As for the rest of the unit, it's a hodgepodge of mid-tier starting transfers from across the P4 and G6, and whatever reserves remain after the portal.

Will this do the job? Who knows? But the situation does give those bearish on Louisville's outlook something to point at. Running backs, no matter how elite, need a good O-line to produce. And while you can out-talent a bad O-line through the passing attack, Kienholz and his crew probably won't be enough, even with Brohm's offensive expertise.

If one or two of the O-line transfers don't pan out, or if Robinson goes down, you could get a repeat of last year, when, in Louisville's first two ACC matches, the line crumbled and Isaac Brown was all but neutralized, rushing for 86 yards on 27 carries and no touchdowns. The line is like a wobbly leg on the otherwise stout chair that is the Cardinal offense. With one bad blow, they could potentially jeopardize the whole operation.

The Cardinals defense, on the other hand, shouldn't encounter such problems. Last year, they were elite, ranking 17th in total defense and 10th against the run. That run defense was anchored by EDGE Clev Lubin, who racked up 13.5 TFLs and 8.5 sacks. He's flanked by AJ Green, who added six TFLs and four sacks of his own. They also added Demco Kennedy and Tyler Thompson in the portal, the former a mid-level starter from Purdue, the latter a DL-LB hybrid from UNC who put up seven sacks and 7.5 TFLs in 2025. Speaking of linebackers, Louisville returns starters Stanquan Clark and T.J. Capers and will look within for depth pieces. The continuity primes an already strong front seven for an even better 2026.

This trend of continuity also extends to the coaching staff, as although defensive coordinators Mark Hagen and Ron English voluntarily stepped away, they were replaced internally, with position coaches Steve Ellis and Mark Ivey promoted to share the role in 2026.

The secondary is a bit of a partial exception, as they did lose three starters to graduation. However, they retain perhaps the most talented members of the group, including headliner Antonio Watts, as well as Tayon Holloway and Jabari Mack. They also collected five P4 transfers, as well as Elon product Bryson Scott.

They avoid Miami altogether, catch Ole Miss, the best team on their schedule, in week 1, and have just five away games, of which the most difficult will likely be the matchup against the Jackets on the Flats. The Cardinals will also have a runway leading to Atlanta, as they play a sorry Syracuse team, get a bye, then play an arguably worse Stanford team before the Jackets. In short, unless the offensive line crumbles or the defense just… stops defending, the Jackets will have their hands full with the Cardinals.

articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars Winners And Losers From Preseason Week 3: Jags Close Strong Behind Rookie Depth
articles.summary: Wortham, Thomas Jr. make strong cases to be included in 53-man roster.
articles.body:
Now that's how you play three phases of preseason football.

The Jacksonville Jaguars took down the visiting Tamp Bay Buccaneers, 19-0, Friday behind three phases of solid play . The Jags got some representative offense, a special teams touchdown and 61-yard field goal as well as a turnover on defense. It was a complete departure from the mess that was the Carolina game.

Are the Jaguars now primed to win the Super Bowl because Wesley Williams and Michael Wortham played well? Who's to say, but at the very least that was a solid way to send this team into the 53-man roster phase ahead of the Week 1 tilt against the Cleveland Browns.

Have a freaking day Bryan Thomas Jr. and Wesley Williams.

Friday night was a feast for two rookie defensive ends in Thomas Jr. (not the wide receiver!) and Williams. The former had 2.5 sacks and two tackles for loss while Williams had two tackles and a fumble recovery.

It was probably always going to be the case that Williams, a fourth round pick out of Duke, was going to make the roster. Not so much for Thomas Jr., but he made a tremendous effort in his final dress rehearsal as to why he should make the 53-man team.

While the Jags may have issues on the backup offensive line front, Tampa Bay certainly does as well and the Jags feasted in the backfield to the tune of five total sacks.

A special shoutout also goes to second-year Auburn man Jalen McLeod who somewhat quietly led the team with seven tackles and one tackle for loss. All three of these guys put great tape out there in the final preseason game and by all counts should continue to rock a Jags jersey.

Speaking of having a day, Wortham really decided he wanted to make the roster too. The rookie out of Montana went out and collected 170 total all-purpose yards including a 63-yard punt return touchdown. He finished tied for first on the team in receiving with three catches for 47 yards.

An emerging question mark from preseason was who could possibly be the Jags number two return man behind Parker Washington? Well, Wortham made an incredibly strong case for it being him moving forward and I don't think any Jags fan would complain after seeing that dude cross the length of the field and turn on the afterburners. It's CJ Williams' or Josh Cameron's backup WR spot to lose, but hey good for Wortham for making people in the front office at leas think about it.

Credit where it's due, the special teams unit blocked the hell out of that punt return and had multiple bodies up to see Wortham to the end zone. That's what you like to see from the backups.

Someone maybe not on the roster bubble but could always use a good showing was Hunter Long. And prior to injury, he looked like a man among boys out there.

Long tied Wortham in yardage with two catches for 47 yards, taking the first offensive possession for the Jags for 34 yards. Long was rumbling and stumbling when he had the ball in his hands, putting up a good showing for why he should be kept around.

After drafting two tight ends in April, Long might be on the outside looking in by default, but he made his case. At the very least, he seems like for the practice squad and for a call-up if a guy goes down. We know he can play and will play hard as hell. He certainly cannot hurt this team by keeping him in Duval.

For all the shit Bradley has gotten, and much of it deserved, hats off to the dude for closing the preseason in the best way possible.

Most of Friday night saw Bradley getting killed by his offensive front, mouthing to himself that he wasn't getting helped and footballs bouncing helplessly out of the reach of receivers who need the catches to make a living. That was until the third quarter.

Bradley and the gang mounted a 14 play (!!) 74-yard touchdown drive that saw Bradley float a pass to DeeJay Dallas for six. For good measure, Bradley ran hard for a two-point conversion that had to just feel euphoric for the dude after all he had been through the past two games and change.

This won't change his fate in the NFL, but the rookie closed strong. He even played hurt as evidenced by his hand being wrapped up on the sideline after his scoring drive. I have given Bradley plenty of grief, but I have to give him his flowers for grinding that score out.

Cam Little and Logan Cooke are good. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

I'm not so certain much of anyone flashed as great backup offensive line options through the length of the preseason outside of rookie Emmanuel Pregnon. The team is getting Cole Van Lanen back which is cause for celebration, but questions still linger about Chuma Edoga and his status which could cause him to miss the roster altogether.

This isn't an inspired group and the backups didn't impress against Tampa Bay, helping give way to four sacks and a moribund 2.8 yards per rush.

Nick Mullens, you're the backup quarterback. Congrats. Buy the Rivalry Jersey now.

Trevor Lawrence needs to stay healthy and this is all for naught, but if there is another nitpick area of concern for the Jags you can make the case that it's the QB2 position. It likely (hopefully) doesn't matter in the long run but Mullens didn't exactly flash on TV. His camp reports were fine so hopefully if he's ever needed facing live game action, he turns to that version of himself.

This franchise goes by the way of Lawrence anyway so if Mullens, or really anybody else, is in it's probably over regardless.

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi explains Savio absence for Tottenham’s clash with Newcastle
articles.summary: Savio scored a debut goal for Spurs in the Carabao Cup but missed out on a Premier League bow through injury
articles.body:
Tottenham have been dealt a cruelly-timed injury blow after Savio was denied a Premier League debut for the club due to a muscular issue.

Savio joined Spurs from Manchester City in an eye-watering £85m deal but got off to a perfect start for the Lilywhites in midweek, coming off the bench and immediately scoring in the 5-0 Carabao Cup win over Charlton .

He was expected to make his league bow for Spurs alongside fellow ex-City team-mate Omar Marmoush against Newcastle in Saturday's late kick-off, but was notable for his absence in the matchday squad.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi has now explained why the Brazilian missed out on the visit of the Magpies.

"We had some bad news yesterday," he told Sky Sports. "He suffered muscular fatigue. The medical staff didn't want to take a risk. I agree with them."

Tottenham will hope Savio's absence from the squad is short-lived, with De Zerbi indicating that his omission was precautionary.

Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti was in the stands at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, potentially with an eye to watch Savio given he would have been the only Brazilian player in either squad, with Joelinton similarly recovering from an injury for the Magpies.

Marmoush did start against Newcastle to make his debut, which was one of five changes De Zerbi made from the Charlton win.

Sandro Tonali was back in midfield to face his former club, while Micky van de Ven, Pedro Porro and Andy Robertson also came into the side.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal took espresso machine from Tigers locker room after trade
articles.summary: Former Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal spoke before Saturday's game at Comerica Park, highlighting what makes the Los Angeles Dodgers successful.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal looked comfortable sitting in the first-base dugout in the stadium he called home for his first seven MLB seasons – minus a few inconveniences that come from playing for the visiting team.

"I've never been on this side of the clubhouse. So when I first got here, I'm like, 'which way is the field?'" he said. "It's much farther down there. There's a lot more steps going on, but I guess it's good for your health."

The setting was familiar, but the threads were not. Skubal wore his usual headband and sleeveless hoodie, but both were dipped in Dodger blue instead of stamped with the Olde English D. The night before, he pitched six brilliant innings in the Dodgers' 2-1 win over the Detroit Tigers , returning to Comerica Park less than a month after the Tigers traded him to Los Angeles at the deadline for three prospects.

See Tarik Skubal take mound in surreal scene in Tigers vs Dodgers at Comerica Park

Skubal didn't have a say in where he went. But based on his interaction with the media before Detroit's game with the Dodgers on Saturday, Aug. 29, he looks to have landed in a situation he really likes.

"[The Dodgers] have won the last two World Series for a reason. It's not a mistake," he said. "You watch [first baseman Freddie Freeman's] ground ball routine, he does the same thing every single day. I think those routines matter, and they translate to the field, stuff they do in the cage, the way pitchers prepare ... no little thing is overlooked, and I think that's what makes good teams really good."

Skubal looked much like himself on Friday, to the mixed emotions of the sold-out crowd that came to see him one last time in 2026. The lefty is aware that him landing on the Dodgers has created strong feelings about competitive balance in MLB, and though he didn't directly answer a question about his place in that narrative, he acknowledged how much those feelings have created intense road atmospheres.

"Both sides benefit from it, just having the energy in the ballpark. That's what fans do," he said. "So I think [the fans] are entitled to whatever opinion they want to have. I appreciate it, because they make these games a ton of fun to play in, no matter where we are."

Skubal may have joined a juggernaut in Los Angeles, but he didn't forget the relationships he made in a more humble spot in Detroit.

"I sent over some stuff this morning, including some donuts, and there was some stuff that I had coming in for a couple of the guys that play golf," he said. "Walking on the field and saying hi to these guys, just getting to see coaches, teammates, support staff and all in between. All those people go out of their way to help me on and off the field. So just kind of show some appreciation when I go say hi to them."

And maybe most important, for clubhouse culture, at least – Skubal finally admitted to taking the espresso machine he bought and shared with his teammates for years.

"I'll wear it," he said, adding that the machine now lives at his house. "I did buy it, but I guess I'll wear it."

Tigers left fielder Riley Greene is one step closer to returning from his hamstring injury.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said before Saturday's game that Greene will play in a rehab game leading off as a designated hitter for Triple-A Toledo tonight in St. Paul, Minnesota. Greene hasn't played since an Aug. 11 win over the Cleveland Guardians, exiting that game with an injured right hamstring. The Tigers placed him on the 10-day IL the next day, and the Tigers have gone 3-12 in his absence.

Greene has been one of the best hitters in Detroit's lineup this season, putting up an .816 OPS over 492 plate appearances. The Tigers could use both his bat and his glove during this stretch, as Detroit's playoff odds have shrunk to low single-digits as the final month of the regular season approaches.

"The hope is that [Greene] is going to get on the field tomorrow in the outfield, and then we'll reassess," Hinch said.

The Tigers travel to play the Minnesota Twins in Minneapolis for a three-game series starting on Monday, Aug. 31, which would line up well for a potential Greene return. But Hinch isn't making any promises.

"In a perfect world that aligns well, but we can't make any assumptions yet," he said.

articles.title: Georgia Bulldogs rated as college football's most talented roster
articles.summary: 247Sports released their talent composition rankings, and the Georgia Bulldogs ranked No. 1 for the second straight year.
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs definitely have the talent to compete for a national championship and 247Sports agrees. They're listed Georgia as the No. 1 team in terms of talent composite in the nation. Georgia has 105 total commits, including 57 that are four-stars and 12 that are five-stars in their database.

This is the second straight season Georgia has been the No. 1 team in talent composition. They were ranked No. 1 in 2025, and they almost proved 247Sports right by winning the SEC. Unfortunately, they lost to the Ole Miss Rebels, who were ranked No. 21 last season, in the Sugar Bowl. The Rebels are now at No. 15.

The Bulldogs added to their No. 1 ranked roster the No. 9 ranked recruiting class in the nation, with several freshman, such as tight end Kaiden Prothro, cornerback Tyriq Green, and interior offensive lineman Zykie Helton expected to take a ton of snaps this season. Georgia's roster building has relied primarily on traditional recruiting as opposed to the transfer portal.

The defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers are nowhere to be found in the top 10, however. In fact, they're all the way at No. 40 this season. They were ranked No. 72 last season, which goes to show what the power of smart recruiting and great coaching can do. Indiana had a lot of continuity and veteran leadership on that roster, and Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza was a transfer from the California Golden Bears.

Rounding out the top 10, there are four other SEC teams ( Alabama , Texas, Texas A&M, LSU). Four other teams come from the Big Ten ( Oregon , Ohio State , USC , Michigan), and Notre Dame, coming in at No. 6, is an independent. Shockingly, there are no ACC or Big 12 teams in the top 10, not even the national championship runner-up Miami Hurricanes or Big 12 champion Texas Tech Red Raiders .

articles.summary: Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana has reportedly accepted a loan move to Galatasaray, and there could be an option to buy attached.The Frenchman is not part o...
articles.body:
Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana has reportedly accepted a loan move to Galatasaray, and there could be an option to buy attached.

The Frenchman is not part of their plans for this season and was cut from the squad over the summer by new coach Ruben Amorim.

He is the one most likely to find a new club , rather than fellow outcasts Fikayo Tomori, Santiago Gimenez and Warren Bondo.

According to transfer pundits Fabrizio Romano and Yagiz Sabuncuoglu , Fofana is eager to make the move to Galatasaray, where he would reunite with Rafael Leao.

There is some dispute over whether this is going to be a pure loan, or with an option to buy attached.

VERONA, ITALY – APRIL 19: Youssouf Fofana of AC Milan is challenged by Jean-Daniel Akpa Akpro of Hellas Verona during the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and AC Milan at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on April 19, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

While the player is ready to come to Istanbul, Milan still need to be convinced, as they would much prefer a permanent sale this summer.

Fofana is under contract at San Siro until June 2028 and has also been targeted by the likes of Brighton and Hove Albion, Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Besiktas.

articles.body:
The Shield is the second piece of silverware of the campaign for the Warriors, who lifted the Challenge Cup at Wembley in May.

They will hope to emulate the success of last season where they completed the same double before tasting Grand Final glory with victory over St Helens .

Topping the table earns Wigan a bye straight through to the showpiece, which will be staged at their own Brick Community Stadium on Sunday September 27, live on Sky Sports with a 5.30pm kick-off.

Their opponents will be decided on September 18, when the sides finishing second and third meet in the semi-final.

The Grand Final forms part of a double-header, with the promotion play-off final staged before the main event as the winners of the Women's Championship face the team finishing fourth in the BWSL Shield competition.

articles.title: Patriots roster cuts tracker: All the latest moves, news, rumors, and more
articles.summary: Tracking New England’s transactions ahead of the upcoming roster deadline
articles.body:
With training camp and the NFL preseason wrapped up, the New England Patriots are on to building their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season.

New England, including the league's other 31 franchises, will need to reduce their rosters from a maximum of 90 to no more than 53 by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30. As a result, hundreds of players will hit the waiver wire and the open market over the next few days, including up to 37 Patriots.

In addition to the roster cuts, a multitude of other transactions, ranging from trades, waiver-wire pickups, free-agent signings and players being moved to injury lists, will be made. To not get lost in all the action, we have you covered: welcome to our annual Patriots roster cuts tracker .

Make sure to bookmark and regularly visit this page, where we will compile all the latest news, rumors and instant analysis in one place. For an up-to-date look at the team's roster, please click here . For all the latest odds about the Patriots' 2026 season, head over to Fanduel Sportsbook .

Latest news at the top. The Patriots had 91 players on their roster coming out of their preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: Final Saints 53-man roster prediction
articles.summary: The 53-man roster deadline is almost here.
articles.body:
We are finally done with preseason, and less than two weeks away from the beginning of the regular season. For the New Orleans Saints, this was a pretty busy training camp with position battles sprinkled throughout the team. Many of these battles did not have clear winners, but the Saints still must figure out who they want to bring in for the season, and here is my attempt to do that.

QB (2): Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler

This was such an interesting position battle because Zach Wilson did look like the better QB in game 1, but it went back to square 1 after game 2. It was such a bad performance by both QBs that any momentum was destroyed. Then, in game 3, Rattler did look like the better QB, and I think the Saints might just go with what they're comfortable with.

RB (5): Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, Audric Estime, and Zamir White

The RBs became such an interesting situation due to the injuries, but hopefully, mostly everyone will be healthy for Game 1. Alvin Kamara's availability is a bit up in the air, so if he hits the IR, I can see this group only being 4 players, and I do see Devin Neal on the IR. I think, given the injury luck this season, bringing 5 guys makes sense, and all of them did really well in game 3 of the preseason.

WR (5): Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, Barion Brown, Bryce Lance, and Kevin Austin Jr.

In this group, I originally had 6 spots filled, but with Jordyn Tyson on IR, I think the Saints are only bringing 5 players as of now. I think the decision comes down to Kevin Austin Jr. or Bub Means, and although Means has done well, the staff really seems to like Austin Jr.

TE (3): Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant, and Oscar Delp

Nothing really changes here, especially with Moliki Matavao out for the season.

OL (9): Kelvin Banks Jr., David Edwards, Erik McCoy, Cesar Ruiz, Taliese Fuaga, Jeremiah Wright, Easton Kilty, William Sherman, and Asim Richards

The starters for this group are the same, but the depth is nearly the opposite of my expectations. Jeremiah Wright just kept improving each game and had a really good performance against the Cowboys. Starting might not be out of the question this season. His spot was expected.

Behind him, Easton Kilty is a decent depth player with potential, William Sherman took over the backup center role, and Asim Richards is just tackle depth. Although I do think the Saints could move on from Richards, a player would need to be coming in before that happens.

DE (6): Chase Young, Carl Granderson, Cam Jordan, Anfernee Jennings, Tyree Wilson, and Michael Heldman

Nothing changes for this group in my prediction. I already believed the Saints would bring 6 edge rushers onto the 53-man roster, and I do think that happens. Wilson had a quiet offseason, but made some plays in the last preseason game. For Heldman, he had some shining moments throughout the entire preseason and got some really good pressures/sacks. The Saints should not risk letting him go.

DT (6): Christen Miller, Vernon Broughton, Nathan Shepherd, Davon Godchaux, John Ridgeway III, and Myles Cole

A lot has changed here due to injuries and some releases, which is why I think the Saints also bring 6 players here. That extra spot was either going to Myles Cole or Jay'Viar Suggs, and it was difficult to choose, but I ended up going with Cole.

LB (5): Kaden Elliss, Pete Werner, Danny Stutsman, Isaiah Stalbird, and Jaylan Ford

It's going to be very interesting to see if the Saints bring 5 or 4 LBs onto the 53-man roster, but with how Ford has done in training camp and preseason, he must be in consideration. For my prediction, I do think the Saints bring him, especially with this room being a bit of a worry going into the season.

CB (4): Kool-Aid McKinstry, Quincy Riley, Martin Emerson, and Jayden Price

Do I like bringing only 4 corners? Absolutely not, but who else has proven themselves to get onto the roster? Price and Emerson have struggled at times, but have also made really good plays. They are good depth to have if an injury occurs and on special teams. The one surprise player on the outside is Isaac Yiadom, but his preseason was not good.

S (5): Justin Reid, Jonas Sanker, Julian Blackmon, Jordan Howden, and Lorenzo Styles Jr.

Styles is injured, and if he starts on the IR, I could see the Saints bring someone else in this group, but I do think he could be good to go. Styles Jr. has shown the ability to bounce back from injury, and roster-wise, will be a major contributor on special teams.

ST (3): Daniel Carlson, Ryan Wright, and Zach Wood

Well, I didn't think Daniel Carlson would be in New Orleans, but here we are. He clearly won the competition against the Cowboys, hitting the game-winning FG and being perfect on the day.

articles.title: UDFA making it 'really difficult' for Jaguars during roster cutdowns
articles.summary: One UDFA is making it "really difficult" for the Jaguars during roster cutdowns.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars' edge rusher Bryan Thomas Jr. is giving Liam Coen and James Gladstone a lot to think about with roster cutdown day looming.

In the Jaguars ' preseason finale against Tampa Bay, Thomas logged five pressures, according to Pro Football Focus, and he was in on three sacks.

"His play style is the right way," Coen said afterward. "It fits a lot of the things that we preach and that we're about as a team. When you have a gift of rushing the passer, man, it's something that you can't ignore. I thought he did some nice things against the run as well tonight. I thought the defense as a whole, obviously with the shutout, was huge, being led by Bryan. He's making it really difficult, which is a good thing. It's just what we're hunting up. He's had that skill set. That was something we really appreciated about his game. He's just continued to do it on this stage."

Despite Thomas' impressive performance, he does still face an uphill battle when it comes to making the 53-man roster. The defensive end group is quite crowded in front of him.

Keeping a seventh defensive end probably isn't in the cards, given the roster impact elsewhere. Has Thomas shown enough to jump Zach Durfee on the depth chart? That's the question that Gladstone and Coen will have to ask themselves.

While preseason performance carries the most weight, for what it's worth, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union posted on X that throughout training camp, he didn't "write down" Thomas' name a lot as those practices unfolded.

The Jaguars signed Thomas after the 2026 draft as a UDFA.
